sub_areas.name: Downtown Grimsby
sub_areas.note: Main Street core south of the QEW around the Christie Street / Ontario Street / Maple Avenue interchange (Wikipedia). OGS point query at 43.1935, -79.5595 returns older alluvial deposits (unit 12: clay, silt, sand, gravel) over Queenston Formation red shale.

sub_areas.name: Grimsby Beach
sub_areas.note: Historic lakeshore neighbourhood of 'gingerbread cottages' on a narrow cul-de-sac street network laid out in 1875 and 1885 subdivision plans, with waterfront access to Lake Ontario (Town of Grimsby page). OGS point query at 43.2085, -79.5215 returned no surficial polygon (point falls at the shoreline); bedrock query returns Queenston Formation.

sub_areas.name: Casablanca
sub_areas.note: West Grimsby around the Casablanca Boulevard QEW interchange, the preferred site for the proposed Grimsby GO station (Wikipedia). OGS point query at 43.1955, -79.6215 returns Paleozoic bedrock at or near surface (unit 3) over Queenston Formation.

sub_areas.name: Winona border
sub_areas.note: Western town limit against Winona (City of Hamilton), around Fifty Road; Winona's centre is at 43.20806, -79.65111 (Wikipedia). OGS point query at 43.212, -79.652 returns Paleozoic bedrock at or near surface (unit 3) over Queenston Formation.

sub_areas.name: Grimsby Mountain (above the escarpment)
sub_areas.note: Rural area on top of the Niagara Escarpment south of the built-up town; the ECCC station 'Grimsby Mountain' sits at 170.6 m elevation. OGS point query at 43.17, -79.56 returns fine-textured glaciolacustrine silt and clay (unit 8a) over Lockport Formation dolostone; a point at 43.183, -79.565 on the escarpment face returns clay-to-silt till (unit 5d) over Lockport.

sub_areas.name: Forty Mile Creek corridor
sub_areas.note: Creek crossing the town from the escarpment to Lake Ontario at the harbour. OGS point query at 43.205, -79.55 near the creek mouth returns Paleozoic bedrock at or near surface (unit 3) over Queenston Formation.

sub_areas.name: East Grimsby (Bartlett Avenue)
sub_areas.note: East end around the Bartlett Avenue QEW interchange (Wikipedia). OGS point query at 43.1985, -79.5165 returns coarse-textured glaciolacustrine sand and gravel (unit 9) over Queenston Formation, the same unit as the town reference coordinate.

bedrock.formation: Queenston Formation (Upper Ordovician) below the Niagara Escarpment; Lockport Formation (Silurian) above it (OGS MRD219).
bedrock.description: Queenston: red shale and siltstone, minor green shale and siltstone, and variable calcareous siltstone to sandstone and limestone interbeds. Lockport (MRD219 subunit 18b): Vinemount shale beds (argillaceous dolostone and shale), Goat Island Member light brown dolostone, and Gasport Member blue-grey dolostone and limestone. OGS point queries return Queenston at all seven points on the lake plain (reference, downtown, Grimsby Beach, Casablanca, Winona border, Forty Mile Creek mouth, Bartlett Avenue) and Lockport at the two points on and above the escarpment (43.183, -79.565 and 43.17, -79.56).
bedrock.depth_note: Depth to bedrock was not retrieved (no drift-thickness dataset queried). OGS surficial mapping shows bedrock at or near surface (unit 3) at the Casablanca, Winona-border and Forty Mile Creek query points; elsewhere on the lake plain bedrock lies beneath glaciolacustrine sand and gravel or alluvium of unstated thickness.

implications_for_piles: The Town of Grimsby's own deck permit checklist states that if helical piers are used, supporting engineering and CCMC approval will be required with the application; the foundation plan must show footing locations, sizes and depths, and the cross section must show the depth and size of piers below grade.

The Town's footing inspection checklist sets the conventional baseline: footing elevation a minimum of 1.2 m below finished grade on solid, clean, unfrozen, undisturbed soil, with a geotechnical engineer's confirmation of design bearing pressure suggested and an engineer's report required where high groundwater is suspected.

OGS maps bedrock at or near surface (unit 3) across west Grimsby (Casablanca, Winona border) and along Forty Mile Creek, over Queenston red shale; shallow shale refusal is a site condition to confirm before installation there. No site-specific depth, torque or capacity figures were retrieved.

Soil texture differs by area: coarse sand and gravel (unit 9) in central and east Grimsby, older alluvium (unit 12) downtown along the creek, and fine silt and clay (unit 8a) above the escarpment on Grimsby Mountain, where the bedrock changes to Lockport dolostone; an engineer's soil-specific determination is not transferable between the lake plain and the mountain.

permits.authority: Town of Grimsby Building Division (the Town's deck handout is headed 'BUILDING DEPARTMENT' and its web page says 'check with your local building department'); Niagara Region is the upper tier and does not issue building permits
permits.deck_permit_required_when: Town residential-permit page: a building permit is required for a deck or porch when the deck is greater than 10 m2 or greater than 0.6 metres in height, and also if the structure is attached to a building or serves as a primary entrance to the house. The Town's Decks and Covered Porches handout lists the triggers as: greater than 10 m2 in area; attached to a building; providing a primary entrance to the house.
permits.footing_depth_requirement: Town Footing Inspection Checklist: 'The elevation of the footings is a minimum of 1.2 m below finished grade level and provides the proper frost protection cover'; footings on solid, clean, unfrozen, undisturbed ground; engineer's report where high groundwater is suspected. Deck checklist: foundation plan must show footing locations, dimensions, sizes and depths; cross section must show depth and size of piers below grade; 'If using helical piers, supporting engineering and CCMC approval will be required.' No numeric deck-footing depth is printed on the deck handout itself; the sample permit drawings PDF is an image-only file and its text was not read.
inspections: Footings (undisturbed soil, minimum footing depth, form layout, footings, waterproofing, surrounding precautions)
permits.fee_note: 2026 Consolidated Fees and Charges, Schedule C - Building: line 10 'Decks, Porches, Accessory Buildings, Carports' $1.12 per ft2 (no HST); minimum fee for a permit $232.00; decks are charged in addition to any floor-area fee on the same application; multiple decks built simultaneously on one property are charged 50% of the applicable fee. Revision fees for 2026: major revision up to 3 hours review $264.00, each hour after $132.00. Fees are payable at application submission.
permits.timeline_note: Town page: if the application is complete, initial review time for residential applications is 10 business days (second units 15, non-residential 20); incomplete applications do not follow these timelines; each resubmission may extend review by two or more weeks. Published average processing time: residential alterations (detached, semi) 7 weeks; new residential 13 weeks.
permits.portal_note: The Town introduced Cloudpermit for 2026 for online submission, payment and inspection requests; the Town's entry page is https://www.grimsby.ca/build-and-invest/building-division/applying-for-a-building-permit/ . Building Division contact: building@grimsby.ca, 905-309-2022; Town Hall 160 Livingston Avenue, Grimsby ON L3M 0J5.

climate.station: Vineland Rittenhouse (Climate ID 6139143; 43.167 N, 79.417 W; about 11 km east-southeast of the Grimsby reference point) for all values; Hamilton A (Climate ID 6153194; 43.172 N, 79.934 W; about 31 km west-southwest) as the nearest 30-year full-record comparison
climate.normals_period: 1981-2010 (ECCC GeoMet climate-normals API). Vineland Rittenhouse normals are computed from 1981-2001 records: 21 years, code C for temperature, code D for the frost-free period. Hamilton A: 30 years, code A. The 1991-2020 normals pages on climate.weather.gc.ca did not return a data table on 2026-09-25 (see notes).
climate.freeze_thaw_note: Vineland Rittenhouse 1981-2010: January mean daily temperature -3.67 C, January mean daily minimum -7.11 C; 23.44 days/yr with daily minimum below -10 C; 0.72 days/yr below -20 C; 46.3 days/yr with daily maximum <= 0 C versus 121.03 days/yr with daily minimum <= 0 C, so roughly 75 days a year cross 0 C between night and day (derived by subtraction); mean last spring frost day 116 (about Apr 26), first fall frost day 291 (about Oct 18); 112.2 cm annual snowfall. Hamilton A 1981-2010 for comparison: January mean -5.5 C, 37.69 days/yr below -10 C, 56.14 days/yr with maximum <= 0 C, 167 frost-free days, 156.5 cm snowfall. The ECCC station 'Grimsby Mountain' (6133055, 170.6 m, recording since 2005) has no published normals.

code.note: The 1.2 m figure is sourced as the minimum footing elevation below finished grade printed on the Town of Grimsby's official Footing Inspection Checklist ('a minimum of 1.2 m below finished grade level and provides the proper frost protection cover'). It is a Town inspection document, not a deck drawing; the Town's deck handout prints no numeric depth and its sample permit drawings PDF is image-only and was not read. The Ontario Building Code clause text itself was NOT retrieved (ontario.ca/laws renders the regulation as a JavaScript shell and the 2024 Building Code Compendium is distributed through Publications Ontario). Do not cite a clause number.
